The determinant and scalar triple product result in the same expression for a 3x3 matrix, so it doesn't matter which one you use.

I think it does not matter if you do it before or after orthogonalization as we're only looking at the sign. I wonder though what happens if you get into float precision issues for really small vectors, so I would say it's safer to do it after orthogonalization.

B.t.w. my code also doesn't handle every case. E.g. If you pass in a matrix where all columns are the same vector then it will happily divide by zero.

I just realized `Basis::determinant()` (which uses cofactor expansion) and the scalar triple product were basically the exact same amount of operations, so suggesting one was cheaper than the other was not very bright of me.

But I guess I should use the scalar triple product anyway, since we don't have the `Basis` object set up right after orthogonalization.
